{"id":"PKIX-vcpy","title":"diff-harness gates main on diagnostic text and has been red since 2026-11-16","description":"## The problem

.github/workflows/diff-harness.yml went red on main around 2026-11-16 and stayed red through at least three main pushes, including today's. Nobody looked. I did not know the workflow existed until I read gh run list after pushing 61 commits on top of it.

A gate that cries wolf stops being read, and then it is worse than no gate: it occupies the slot where a real signal would go.

## Why it is red, and why that is the gate's fault

Two causes, both third-party rather than pkix-path.

1. EIGHT CHAINS DRIFTED Agreement -> DiagnosticDivergence (71 -> 63 and 49 -> 58 against pkix-difftest/baseline-pkits.json).

   Class::DiagnosticDivergence means "everyone agrees on Pass/Fail but differs on the reason". So no verdict changed. pkix-path decided the same thing about every chain; only the oracles' error WORDING moved. Near-certainly an OpenSSL or pyca version bump on the runner.

   The harness already documents this exposure in its own workflow comment: "The diff harness's verdicts are sensitive to the exact OpenSSL build (option string parsing, error wording) and pyca release." The gate was built knowing it would drift, and then pinned the drift-prone values in a committed baseline anyway.

2. TWO HARNESS ERRORS, each an oracle limitation rather than a defect:
   - pyca on "4.1.5 Valid DSA Parameter Inheritance Test5" -- pyca's ASN.1 parser rejects an SPKI with inherited/absent DSA parameters.
   - pkix-path on "4.2.3 Valid pre2000 UTC notBefore Date Test3" -- der 0.8.3 cannot represent a pre-1970 UTCTime. See PKIX-str9; fail-closed, no security impact.

   Both surface as anonymous "harness error(s) during run; chains skipped from classification", so they look like breakage rather than known gaps.

## What to decide

The gate's job is catching pkix-path regressions. It currently also catches OpenSSL and pyca release notes. Options, roughly in order of how much they are worth:

- PIN THE ORACLE VERSIONS. Install a fixed OpenSSL and a pinned pyca/cryptography in the job rather than taking whatever ubuntu-latest ships. Makes the baseline meaningful; costs a periodic deliberate bump, which is the right place for that cost.
- COMPARE VERDICT CLASSES, NOT DIAGNOSTIC TEXT. Treat Agreement and DiagnosticDivergence as one bucket for gating purposes, since neither represents a verdict disagreement. Keeps the signal that matters (LooserThanWild, StricterThanWild, OracleDivergence) and drops the one that drifts. Cheapest real fix.
- MAKE KNOWN GAPS EXPLICIT. An expected-failure list, so 4.1.5 and 4.2.3 stop reading as errors and a NEW harness error is visible again.
- FAIL LOUDLY OR NOT AT ALL. If the gate stays drift-prone, it should not gate main. A scheduled run that opens an issue would be more honest than a red X everyone learns to scroll past.

## Also worth checking

Whether anything else regressed during the week the gate was red. The drift analysis above says verdicts did not change, which is reassuring, but it was derived from log lines rather than from a clean local run with pinned oracles. Worth one deliberate run to confirm before trusting it.

## Acceptance

[ ] Root cause of the 8-chain drift confirmed (oracle version bump, or something else)
[ ] Gate redesigned so a third-party version bump cannot make it red
[ ] 4.1.5 and 4.2.3 recorded as expected gaps rather than anonymous harness errors
[ ] diff-harness green on main, and a note on what it will and will not catch","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-25T02:42:40.145390581Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-25T02:42:40.145390581Z"}

{"notes":"CORRECTION 2026-11-25. My "the drift is benign" claim was WRONG. I derived it from four grepped log lines and missed the two classes that matter.

## The real summary diff

  class                  baseline    CI
  Agreement                    71    63
  DiagnosticDivergence         49    58
  LooserThanWild               81    93   <-- +12, and this is rank 0, the WORST class
  StricterThanWild             46    33   <-- -13
  OracleDivergence              0     0
  total                       247   247

Both sides sum to 247, so no chains appeared or vanished. Thirteen chains left StricterThanWild: twelve became LooserThanWild and one joined the agreed bucket.

LooserThanWild means pkix-path ACCEPTS a chain an oracle REJECTS. Twelve more of those is the exact signal this gate exists to produce, and it is the dangerous direction.

## What I got wrong, and how

I previously wrote in this bead and in a pushed commit message that "no verdict changed, pkix-path decided the same thing about every chain" and that the cause was near-certainly an OpenSSL or pyca version bump.

That came from grepping the CI log for Agreement and DiagnosticDivergence, seeing those two move, and reasoning about what DiagnosticDivergence means. The grep never showed me LooserThanWild or StricterThanWild. Verdicts changed for twenty-five chains.

The lesson is narrow and I keep relearning it today: a filtered view of evidence is not the evidence. I filtered, concluded, and published the conclusion.

## What is actually established

- 25 chains changed class: 13 out of StricterThanWild, 12 into LooserThanWild, net +1 into the agreed bucket
- total is unchanged at 247, so the corpus is intact
- OracleDivergence remains 0, so the oracles still agree with each other

## What is NOT established

WHETHER pkix-path changed or the oracles did. Both produce this shape:

- If pkix-path became more permissive, chains it used to fail now pass, moving Stricter -> Looser.
- If pyca or OpenSSL became STRICTER, chains they used to pass now fail while pkix-path still passes, which also moves Stricter -> Looser without pkix-path changing at all.

The second is quite plausible -- pyca has been tightening extension handling, and the baseline already shows pyca rejecting unaccounted-for critical extensions on many chains. But I asserted an oracle bump once already today on thin evidence and will not do it again.

The failures began around 2026-11-16, which predates this session's work.

## How to settle it

Run the harness locally against known oracle versions and compare against the baseline. If local matches the baseline, the runner's oracles changed. If local reproduces the CI numbers, pkix-path changed and the next step is bisecting which commit moved those twelve chains.

The gate fix landed separately and does NOT paper over this: LooserThanWild and StricterThanWild are still gated individually, so the job correctly stays red until this is explained.

## Revised acceptance

[ ] Determine whether pkix-path or the oracles moved, by running the harness locally against pinned oracle versions
[ ] If pkix-path: identify the commit and decide whether the new behaviour is correct (a baseline update) or a regression (a fix)
[ ] If the oracles: pin their versions in the job, so the baseline means something
[ ] Name the twelve chains that moved into LooserThanWild -- they are the ones that matter, not the counts
[ ] 4.1.5 and 4.2.3 recorded as expected gaps rather than anonymous harness errors
[ ] diff-harness green on main, with a note on what it will and will not catch","priority":1,"title":"diff-harness: 12 chains moved into LooserThanWild; cause unestablished, red since 2026-11-16"}
